interest: Shows a 1930s dispute over a Japanese immigrant's bank deposits devalued by the yen, testing US jurisdiction over foreign banks.
keywords: Treaty of Commerce and Navigation of 1911
overview: This file (894.51611/1–2) centers on an inquiry submitted to Secretary of State Henry L. Stimson by Philadelphia attorney Daniel R. Rothermel concerning the legal status and operations of the Yokohama Specie Bank, Ltd. in New York. Rothermel represented the court-appointed guardian of Shoraku Maki (alias Samuel Mack), an incapacitated Japanese national institutionalized in Philadelphia, who held yen certificates of deposit that the bank's New York agency refused to redeem in dollars at pre-depreciation exchange rates, eventually insisting that payment could only be made in Japan. The file includes Rothermel's detailed petition and follow-up inquiry, an internal Department of State Legal Adviser memorandum prepared for Eugene H. Dooman advising on jurisdictional limitations, and the official departmental reply signed by Stanley K. Hornbeck disclaiming federal regulatory authority over banking, referring the complainant to New York State banking authorities, and citing Article VII of the 1911 Treaty of Commerce and Navigation with Japan.

subfiles.about: Inquiry from an attorney requesting State Department intervention regarding the refusal of the Yokohama Specie Bank in New York to honor certificates of deposit held by an incapacitated Japanese national.
subfiles.summary: Rothermel seeks Stimson's help after Yokohama Specie Bank repeatedly refused to redeem an incompetent client's deposit certificates at pre-devaluation rates, demanding presentation in Japan instead.
subfiles.title: Letter from Daniel R. Rothermel to Secretary of State Henry L. Stimson regarding deposits of Shoraku Maki in the Yokohama Specie Bank

subfiles.about: Department of State reply informing Rothermel that the federal government lacks regulatory authority over banking institutions and citing the 1911 commercial treaty with Japan.
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck (for the Secretary of State)
keywords: Treaty of Commerce and Navigation of 1911
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck tells Rothermel State has no jurisdiction over banks, citing Treaty of 1911's Article VII making foreign banks' business subject to local law, and refers him to New York authorities.
subfiles.title: Letter from Stanley K. Hornbeck to Daniel R. Rothermel regarding the legal status and regulation of Japanese branch banks

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum from the Legal Adviser recommending specific additions and treaty citations for the Department's draft reply to Daniel R. Rothermel.
keywords: Treaty of Commerce and Navigation of 1911
subfiles.summary: Legal Adviser's office drafts a reply to Rothermel summarizing the bank's refusal to pay, disclaiming federal banking jurisdiction, and citing Treaty of 1911's Article VII.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from the Legal Adviser to Eugene H. Dooman (Division of Far Eastern Affairs) regarding draft reply to Daniel R. Rothermel

subfiles.about: Follow-up inquiry asking whether the State Department received Rothermel's November 21 letter and when a response may be expected.
subfiles.summary: Rothermel asks State whether his November letter on the Shoraku Maki case was received and when to expect a reply.
subfiles.title: Letter from Daniel R. Rothermel to Secretary of State Henry L. Stimson inquiring about status of earlier correspondence
